findings.reason: Confirmed on all three sources, read at the cited places, and the finding's own scoping claim verified too. The audit's duplicate note for the upstream EllipticCurves Layer 4 entry reads 'Owns Tate's algorithm over a DVR, the algorithmic (Ogg) exponent v(Delta) - m + 1 and its identification with the ramification-theoretic conductor, and Neron-Ogg-Shafarevich; that identification is the elliptic-curve conductor comparison asked ...'. The upstream document says the opposite in terms. It first separates the two notions — the algorithmic (Ogg) exponent is 'called that, not "the conductor", until identified with the ramification-theoretic conductor' — and then excludes the identification explicitly: 'The ramification-theoretic conductor and its identification with this algorithmic f_p ... is a separate, related project, cited (Saito) for context only'. That is an explicit exclusion rather than silence about a prerequisite, which is the distinction the finding rests on and it is the right one. The scoping is also exactly as claimed, and I checked it rather than taking it: R01.3's target 'Comparison with the conductor of an elliptic curve, including wild contributions at 2 and 3' carries library 'absent', and the layer verdict is 'not built'. So nothing would be wrongly built from this error; what it risks is a worker skipping a comparison the audit tells them is already owned upstream — the note even asserts 'that identification is the elliptic-curve conductor comparison asked' for. Medium is the right severity for that. One refinement to carry into the fix, from the upstream document itself: it locates the historical gap more precisely than the finding does. Both residue characteristics 2 and 3 bring wild complications, but 'only the mixed characteristic (0, 2) case was missing from Ogg's proof: Silverman does residue characteristic 3 and refers 2 to Saito (Duke 1988), whose arithmetic-surface proof is uniform in the residue characteristic'. The fix's phrase 'including wild contributions at 2 and 3' is correct as a statement of the obligation, and adding the literature split would tell the eventual worker where each case comes from. The proposed replacement note is otherwise accurate and I would apply it as written, together with its instruction to keep the target absent, keep the layer not built, and refresh the matching entry in the integrated coverage data rather than removing the comparison from planning.
